alloy.preparation: F460B (Table 3 base alloy F460). 50 gm heats were levitation melted into flat slabs (1/4 x 1 x 1 1/2 inches). All cast slab surfaces were ground to remove imperfections and provide rolling surfaces; the slabs were annealed for 16 hours at 1200 °C (2192 °F) in argon, then hot rolled at 1090 °C (1994 °F) to 1/16 inch thickness. Oxide scale was removed by sand blasting before final annealing. The B-series final heat treatment was 1 hour at 1049 °C (1920 °F), followed by water quenching (PDF p. 4). Discs were spark cut from the resulting strips for polarization measurements (PDF p. 2).

test_solution.preparation: Deaerated synthetic seawater. Before polarization, the seawater was treated with sulfuric acid to neutralize bicarbonate alkalinity and subsequently boiled to remove free carbon dioxide and dissolved oxygen. The pH was adjusted to 7.2 ± 0.2 at 90 °C (PDF pp. 2-3). The synthetic-seawater recipe and chloride-ion concentration are not specified.

test_method.procedure_description: Table 5 run 1108, sample F460B: conventional potentiodynamic anodic polarization in deaerated synthetic seawater at 90 °C and pH 7.2 ± 0.2, at 10 mV/min until a sudden increase in specimen current indicated E_c^scan. Scan start/stop limits and pre-hold are not specified. Potentials are reported versus SCE; polarization-cell/equipment details are referred to earlier publications rather than restated (PDF p. 3).
test_method.pitting_criterion: Sudden increase in specimen current during the anodic scan, identifying E_c^scan.

experiments.result_note: Separate run/method retained; scan and scratch are not interchangeable. Composition is the nominal Table 3 composition (Wt %) for the base alloy identifier, not the rounded Fe-Cr-Mo coordinates or group additions in Fig. 2. Table dashes are not interpreted as zero, and numerical Fe is transcribed rather than balanced. The authors state that E_c^scan depends on procedure, surface finish and polarization rate, and use it only as a reference for subsequent tests.
